newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei finishes down, but well off lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei finishes down, but well off lows.

text.p: Tokyo's Nikkei average finished down on Thursday afternoon but well off lows posted early in the afternoon, brokers said. They said that buying by investment trusts helped the key index recoup some losses after it slipped beneath 19,000 for the first time in over a year.

In other indices, TOPIX lost 9.42 points or 0.64 percent to land at 1,460.01. The Nikkei 300 shed 1.59 points or 0.57 percent to rest at 278.30. The second section index fell 5.37 points or 0.29 percent to 1,815.69. Turnover was 11.45 million shares against 10.34 million on Wednesday.
The most heavily traded issues was Yaohan Japan Corp which gained 32 yen to 448 yen on bargain-hunting in a trade of 6.15 million shares.
Industrial Bank of Japan slumped to a low for the year of 1,990 yen, after losing 30 yen.
It was dragged down by the news that non-bank lender Koei Corp was seeking liquidation under court protection by the end of March, brokers said. IBJ is a major creditor of Koei Corp.
"IBJ shares were dented by the news, but the impact was not startling enough to contribute to the overall weakness of the market," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager, said.
Brokers added that news that Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd would provide 150 billion yen in financial support to one of its group companies was not seen as a depressing factor.
"Yamaichi is not the first do undergo such measures and the market has already factored it in," one broker said.
Yamaichi shares finished down two yen at 503 yen.
The over-the-counter index was down 5.49 points or 0.42 percent at 1,316.25 in late Tokyo afternoon.
